title: Short-Term Business Loans: 3 to 24 Month Funding
seo_title: Short-Term Business Loans: Terms & Payments | Fidelity Funding
meta_description: Short-term business loans typically run 3 to 24 months with daily or weekly payments. See how they work, what they cost, and when they make sense.
keywords: short term loans for small business
dek: Fast, compact financing repaid in months, not years. Understand the payment rhythm, the true cost and the uses that suit it.
intro: Some needs have a clear start and finish: stock up before a trade show, cover a payroll gap until a big invoice lands, or grab a supplier discount that expires Friday. A five-year loan feels wrong for those. A short-term business loan matches the money to the moment.

These loans usually run from about three to twenty-four months, with payments collected daily, weekly or sometimes monthly. The tight schedule is what keeps the term short, and it is also what makes the cost and the cash-flow impact worth examining carefully.

sections.h2: How a short-term loan is structured
paragraphs: You receive a lump sum and repay principal plus a fixed finance charge over a brief period. Some partners express cost as an interest rate, others as a flat fee or factor, so the number you see is not always comparable between offers.

Because the schedule is compressed, each payment is a bigger slice of the total than in a long-term loan. The benefit is that the debt is finished quickly and you can often renew or move on. The drawback is that the payments continue regardless of whether the opportunity paid off.

Payment frequency is the single most important structural detail. Daily payments are pulled by ACH on business days and suit businesses with steady daily deposits, like retail or restaurants. Weekly payments give contractors and service firms a little more breathing room between debits. Monthly payments are the easiest to manage but are more common in longer terms and for stronger credit.

Take a $30,000 loan with a total payback of $35,400 over 24 weeks. That is $1,475 per week. Over a typical month you would pay roughly $5,900, which needs to fit alongside rent, payroll and supplier bills. The figures are illustrative; actual pricing depends on the partner, term and your profile.
The strongest use cases are ones that pay themselves back within the term.
bullets: Buying inventory ahead of a known busy period
Bridging receivables that are confirmed but slow to arrive
Covering a one-time repair or compliance cost
Taking advantage of a bulk or early-payment supplier discount

sections.h2: Uses that tend to go badly
paragraphs: Using short-term debt to fund something that pays back slowly is a mismatch. A renovation that will not increase revenue for a year, or a long-term equipment purchase, is usually better placed on a longer schedule. Likewise, repeatedly renewing a short loan to cover ongoing losses compounds the problem rather than fixing it. If you notice you are borrowing each month just to make the last payment, step back and talk through restructuring with a specialist.

sections.h2: Qualifying and what to have ready
paragraphs: Funding partners offering short-term loans commonly look at time in business, monthly revenue, recent bank statements and credit. Many are comfortable with newer or lower-credit businesses than banks are, provided deposits are steady. Gather three to six months of statements, ID, and basic ownership documents to speed things up.
Expect the amount to be tied to your revenue. A common approach caps financing at a fraction of average monthly deposits, though each partner sets its own rules.

sections.h2: A quick stress test before you accept
paragraphs: Before saying yes, run three simple checks. First, divide the total payback by the number of payments to get the exact debit, then multiply by the payments in a typical month. Second, subtract that figure from your lowest recent month of deposits, not your best one, and see what is left for payroll and rent. Third, ask what happens if one payment bounces: some agreements charge a fee, some trigger default language, and some simply continue.

Say your weakest recent month had $62,000 in deposits and your new loan would take $7,000 that month. That is roughly 11 percent of the weakest-month deposits. If your fixed costs already consume most of the remainder, the loan is probably too heavy even if the offer was approved. A smaller amount or a longer term, if available, may be the safer choice. These figures are hypothetical and meant only to show the method.

Line up offers by total repayment, payment amount, frequency, number of payments, any fees deducted from the proceeds, and prepayment terms. A lower payment spread over more weeks can cost more in total, so look at both numbers.

key_takeaways: Short-term loans typically run about 3 to 24 months with daily or weekly payments.
Payment frequency shapes your cash flow as much as the total cost does.
Best used for needs that repay themselves within the term, such as seasonal inventory or bridging confirmed receivables.
Compare total repayment, fees and prepayment terms across offers.

faq.q: How short is a short-term business loan?
faq.a: Terms commonly range from roughly three months to twenty-four months, though definitions vary by funding partner. The shorter the term, the larger each payment relative to the amount borrowed, so confirm the schedule fits your deposits. What you are actually offered for a short-term loan comes down to your own documents, deposits and circumstances.

faq.q: Why are payments daily or weekly?
faq.a: Frequent payments let the funder reduce exposure over a short term and align with how revenue arrives. They also make the cash impact more constant. Some partners offer monthly options for qualified businesses, so ask what is available for your profile.

faq.q: Are short-term loans more expensive than bank loans?
faq.a: Often yes, in annualized terms, because the repayment period is short and underwriting is faster and more flexible. They may still be the right call when speed matters. Compare total dollars repaid, not just the headline rate or factor. Talking briefly with a specialist can show whether a short-term loan or a bank product is the more realistic match for you.

faq.q: Can I pay a short-term loan off early?
faq.a: It depends on the agreement. Some offer a discount for early payoff, others charge the full finance cost regardless. Ask for the prepayment language in writing before signing. Before agreeing to any prepayment terms, read the whole contract and consider asking a CPA or attorney to look it over.

faq.q: Can I get another loan while repaying one?
faq.a: Some partners allow renewals once a portion is repaid, while others limit additional borrowing. Taking multiple obligations at once can strain cash flow, so weigh the combined daily or weekly payment carefully. Since stacking short-term obligations affects each business differently, a specialist can run through the combined payments against your revenue.
